Timeline::ticks¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<std::int64_t> Timeline::ticks() const

What It Does¶

ticks() exports every temporal position into one owning C++ vector of UTC epoch-nanosecond ticks. Values are emitted in logical row-major order: the last axis changes fastest, then the next-to-last axis, and so on.

The method always flattens. It preserves value order and exact 64-bit precision, but not shape. Record sizes() separately when the receiver will need to reconstruct an N-dimensional timeline, or use epoch_nanos() when a shape-preserving Series is more useful.

Timezone conversion does not change this output because conversion changes wall-clock presentation, not the represented instants.

Returns¶

An owning std::vector<std::int64_t> with exactly numel() entries. A NaT position becomes Timeline::kNaT.

Examples¶

Example 1. Export a vector of exact ticks.

auto times = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-02-29T12:30:00Z",
    "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z",
});
auto ticks = times.ticks();

std::cout << '[' << ticks[0] << ',' << ticks[1] << "]\n";

Output¶

[1709209800000000000,1709251200000000000]

Example 2. A matrix flattens in logical row-major order, including absent positions.

auto matrix = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-02-29T12:30:00Z", "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z"},
    {"2024-03-02T06:15:00Z", ""},
});
auto ticks = matrix.ticks();

std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < ticks.size(); ++i) {
    if (i != 0) std::cout << ',';
    std::cout << ticks[i];
}
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1709209800000000000,1709251200000000000,1709360100000000000,-9223372036854775808]

Example 3. Presentation-zone conversion leaves the exported instant intact.

auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto local = utc.tz_convert("America/New_York");
std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << (utc.ticks() ==
              local.ticks()) << "\n";

Output¶

true

Example 4. Preserve the shape beside the flat values for round-trip work.

auto source = pluss::timeline::epoch({2, 3});
auto ticks = source.ticks();
std::vector<std::int64_t> shape(source.sizes().begin(), source.sizes().end());
auto rebuilt = pluss::timeline::from_epoch(ticks, shape);

std::cout << "source numel=" << source.numel()
          << ", rebuilt dim=" << rebuilt.dim()
          << ", rebuilt numel=" << rebuilt.numel() << "\n";

Output¶

source numel=6, rebuilt dim=2, rebuilt numel=6

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Shape is not encoded in the returned vector.

  • Values are UTC epoch ticks even when tz() names another zone.

  • NaT is an absent-instant sentinel, not an omitted element.

  • The method allocates and copies. Repeated calls create repeated vectors.

  • Calling it on an invalid object state throws rather than returning an empty vector.
